sections.title: Self-paced learning, live webinars, and peer mentorship.
sections.subtitle: Capability building for officers and civil society — built around the way public service work is actually done, not the way textbooks describe it.

sections.title: Capability is the binding constraint.
body: Every governance reform we have studied — without exception — has been bottlenecked at some point on capability. Not money, not technology, not even political will. Capability.

The Learning Hub is our small contribution to that bottleneck. It is free, practitioner-led, and designed around the actual decisions an officer or activist will face — not the ones a textbook expects them to face.

sections.title: Short courses you can do on a Saturday morning
sections.subtitle: Each module is structured as 4–6 short videos, a downloadable reader, and a self-check exercise. No fees. No certifications. Just better practice.

items.title: Systems Thinking in Governance
items.subtitle: 5 modules · ~3 hours
items.description: How to see a public problem as a system — with feedback loops, delays, and unintended consequences — and design interventions that account for the whole.

items.title: Design Thinking for Public Services
items.subtitle: 4 modules · ~2.5 hours
items.description: How to design public services that start with the citizen's day — with case studies from grievance, ration, and certificate services.

items.title: Ethical Public Leadership
items.subtitle: 6 modules · ~4 hours
items.description: Frameworks, codes, and case studies on the everyday dilemmas of public service. With reflections from serving and retired senior officers.

items.title: Citizen Charters that Work
items.subtitle: 3 modules · ~2 hours
items.description: How to design, publish and enforce a citizen charter — with templates, SLAs, and redressal flows.

items.title: Data for Public Decisions
items.subtitle: 4 modules · ~3 hours
items.description: From dashboards to decisions — designing data products that actually shape weekly review meetings, not just annual reports.

items.title: Disaster Preparedness for Districts
items.subtitle: 5 modules · ~3.5 hours
items.description: Pre-positioning, command rooms, citizen communication, and lessons from Kerala Rescue and Covid Jagrata.

sections.title: Upcoming sessions
sections.subtitle: Live, practitioner-led, recorded for later. Register through the form on each session.

items.title: The first 90 days as a district officer
items.description: What to read, who to meet, what to fix first — drawn from senior officers' first-quarter playbooks.

items.title: Designing a citizen charter that closes loops
items.description: A working session on writing a department charter with SLAs, redressal flows and review cadence.

items.title: Convergence in a district — a practical clinic
items.description: How to align health, education and livelihood programmes at the same address — with case examples.

items.title: Public communication for officers
items.description: What to say, when to say it, and the difference between communication and PR.

sections.title: Mentorship by peer officers and senior practitioners
body: The Mentorship Programme matches a mentee — a junior officer, a fellow, an intern, or a civil-society practitioner — with a senior who has done the work. Six conversations, six weeks, real momentum.
Mentors are serving and retired officers, programme leads, and senior academics. The matching is by topic, geography and stage of career.
bullets: Structured around the mentee's actual work, not generic curriculum
Open to officers, fellows, interns and civil-society practitioners

sections.title: Want to mentor or teach a module?
sections.body: Surajyapatham is built on practitioner generosity. If you have a topic you've lived and want to share, write to us — we'll help you shape it into a module or mentorship slot.

sections.title: Pick one module. Block ninety minutes. Begin.
sections.subtitle: The hardest part is not starting. Pick a module that maps to a decision you'll make next quarter — and start there.
